title: Give employees long service leave
what: Give each employee long service leave (or payment in lieu) once they reach the qualifying period of service, and keep long service leave records.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (Tas)
sources.quote: Subject to this Act, an employee is entitled to long service leave on ordinary pay in respect of continuous employment with an employer.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (Tas)
sources.quote: An employer shall keep or cause to be kept a long service leave record in such form as may be prescribed and containing the prescribed particulars.

administration.who: Inspectors under the Industrial Relations Act 1984 (Tas)

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (Tas)
sources.quote: A person who is an inspector under the Industrial Relations Act 1984 is, by virtue of his office, an inspector for the purposes of this Act.

reach.note: Every employer of employees in Tasmania covered by the Act.

sources.title: Long Service Leave Act 1976 (Tas)
sources.quote: Subject to this Act, an employee is entitled to long service leave on ordinary pay in respect of continuous employment with an employer.

assessment.summary: Employers must give long service leave after a long period of service with them. The entitlement builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which ties workers to employers; it also adds record keeping.

marks.reason: Leave builds up with one employer and is mostly lost on moving, which discourages job changes (unlike portable schemes).

assessment.confidence_note: Marked from the law's design against the framework's guide; no evaluation of state long service leave and job mobility was found.
